free_tier.stated: Site claim, quoted: "2 vCPU and 2 GB RAM", "KVM", "No card, no trial that expires into a bill", three regions, since 2013. Multiple independent reports describe an SMS-verification wall and an ad-click requirement with no credentials issued.

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
chaining: Nothing, because the machine is not issued. Any chain through it fails at provisioning.
limits_note: Independent reports say the deployment never yields a root password after the SMS step, so the capacity exists only as a claim; the site also asks users to click advertising links to activate service.
binding_note: Independent reports say the deployment never yields a root password after the SMS step, so the capacity exists only as a claim; the site also asks users to click advertising links to activate service.

identity_cost.detail: no card, but a phone wall: the site claims "No card, no trial that expires into a bill", while users report an SMS verification step after the VPS is created, one of them producing a machine but never a password, and reviews describe a requirement to click advertising links to activate. The record does not state which numbers the SMS check accepts, which is why the kind is any-phone rather than country-phone; no hold or authorisation is stated, and debit or prepaid do not arise because no card is taken

evidence.proved: front page advertises 2 vCPU and 2 GB RAM KVM with no card and root SSH, quoted, and states the model is advertising-funded
users report being asked for SMS verification after creating a VPS, and one reports that the deployment produced a machine but never a password
reviews describe being required to click advertising links to activate the service
a 2023 review calls the site an ad farm that requests significant personal information
the owner identity is hidden in WHOIS and negative reviews were detected, though the site is rated probably not a scam

notes: The site's own page is well written and states the parameters plainly, which is why it keeps appearing in listicles. Two independent user reports plus a review site plus a hidden WHOIS is enough to record it as non-delivering rather than to repeat 2 vCPU as capacity. One testimonial blog claims a 30-day run with a live Discord bot; it is unverifiable and reads as promotional.
